title: Leonard Feather's claim Lee upbraided Lester
summary: Lee rejects the word upbraiding for his advice to his older brother, saying Lester was an artist and not a businessman.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Leonard Feather says that right before he went back to Paris, that you went to New York, and I believe the word he used was that you had 'upbraided him' or not taking care of business, and told him to straighten up or something. Is that true?

Yeah, well, you know, you got to remember that he was my older brother, and as far as the word -- I think that's a bad word, 'upbraiding' him, because I would not do that with him, because I had an awful lot of respect for him.

Because it was our teaching, you know ... no, I couldn't do it. It was done, but it was not done in that manner. It's a bad choice of words. But it's just -- well, he was not a good businessman, you know; he was just a true artist. And they could take advantage of him from every angle that you could think of, you know.
